text:
North Korea on Monday celebrated the country's Mothers' Day, praising women as "real revolutionaries" and "patriots," and noting that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un has elevated their status to the "highest level."
In an article honoring mothers, the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) stressed the crucial role of mothers in the country, saying they are getting respect and love in a social atmosphere that honors mothers devoted to their families and society.
It also pointed out leader Kim's efforts to recognize mothers' dedication to society, including creating Mothers' Day and instituting an honorary award for mothers who have contributed to enhancing the country's prosperity.
The Rodong Sinmun, the official daily of the ruling Workers' Party of Korea, enumerated major party policies on provincial development, healthcare, childcare and education in an article, claiming they are meant to address issues that mothers eagerly hope to resolve.
It also claimed Kim has raised mothers' status to the "highest level."
In a separate article, the newspaper highlighted the propaganda activities of the country's female socialist union, portraying women as "real revolutionaries" and "ardent patriots."
On Nov. 16, 1961, then leader and national founder Kim Il-sung delivered an address on mothers' duties in educating children at a nationwide mothers' conference. North Korea designated the day as Mothers' Day in 2012 and has since observed it.
